answer: Clock-skew fingerprints: each ID's heartbeat pulse carries its local timestamp, and validators fit that machine's crystal drift over 48 epochs. Real oscillators differ by ppm-scale amounts (Kohno et al. measured skew remotely in 2005); clones on one host share one slope. Proposed rule: IDs whose skew matches within 0.5 ppm share one payout. A farmer can whisper a fake offset, but holding a stable, distinct drift per clone is costly, so a server farm is no oasis.
